project.name: demo
project.about: Borrowbox is the lending desk of a neighbourhood tool library: members sign up, find a drill or a ladder in the catalog, borrow it at the counter and bring it back on time.
principles: Works When the Wi-Fi Does Not

items.title: I. The Counter Comes First
items.markdown: Every feature must work for a volunteer standing at the counter with a queue in front of them. A lending step that takes more than three taps, or needs a manual to explain, is not finished.

items.title: II. A Loan Is Never Lost
items.markdown: The record of who holds which tool is the one thing the library cannot rebuild from memory. Every change to a loan is written before it is confirmed on screen, and no feature may delete loan history.

items.title: III. Works When the Wi-Fi Does Not
items.markdown: The library sits in a basement. Checkout and return must work offline on the counter tablet and sync later without asking the volunteer to resolve anything.

items.title: IV. Ask for Less
items.markdown: Members give a name and one way to reach them. A feature that wants more personal data must say in its spec what it is for and when it is deleted.

items.title: V. Tests Before Shelves
items.markdown: A user story is built only after a failing test describes it. Tests run against a real database, not a mock of one.

items.title: VI. Plain Words
items.markdown: Screens, messages and specs use the words volunteers use: tool, loan, member, due date. No internal identifiers on screen, no jargon in reminders.

items.label: Stack
items.value: TypeScript on the server and in the counter app, PostgreSQL for storage

items.label: Hosting
items.value: One small server paid for by the library association

items.label: Accessibility
items.value: WCAG 2.2 AA for every screen a member sees

items.label: Languages
items.value: English and Dutch from the first release

items.title: Sign up at the counter
items.why: Nobody can borrow anything before they are a member.
items.test: Register a person with a name and a phone number, then find them in the member list.

scenarios.given: a person who is not a member
scenarios.when: the volunteer enters their name and phone number
scenarios.then: a member card number is shown and the member appears in the list

scenarios.given: a phone number that already belongs to a member
scenarios.then: the existing member is shown instead of a second record

scenarios.given: the tablet is offline
scenarios.then: the member is saved on the tablet and synced when the connection returns

items.rest: A volunteer registers a new member while the person is standing at the counter.

items.title: Accept the house rules
items.why: The association needs proof that the rules were accepted, but signup works without it for a first loan.
items.test: Sign up a member, accept the rules, and see the date of acceptance on their profile.

scenarios.given: a member who has not accepted the rules
scenarios.when: they tick the box and confirm
scenarios.then: the date is stored on their profile

scenarios.given: the rules text has changed since a member accepted it
scenarios.when: that member next borrows a tool
scenarios.then: they are asked to accept the new text

blocks.heading: Edge Cases
blocks.markdown:
- Two volunteers register the same person on two tablets while both are offline.
- A member has no phone and gives an email address instead.

items.text: System MUST create a member from a name and one contact detail (phone or email)
System MUST refuse a second member with the same contact detail and show the existing one
System MUST give every member a card number that fits on a printed label
System MUST record the date and the version of the house rules a member accepted
System MUST let a volunteer register a member while offline

blocks.heading: Complexity Tracking
blocks.markdown:
| Violation | Why needed | Simpler alternative rejected because |
|---|---|---|
| A second copy of the catalog on the tablet | Search must work offline | Server-only search fails in the basement |

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: Search runs in the counter app on a local mirror of the catalog.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: The basement connection drops several times a day, and 2,000 tools fit in memory with room to spare.

fields.label: Alternatives considered
fields.value: PostgreSQL full-text search on the server (fast, but useless offline); a hosted search service (a monthly bill and member queries leaving the building).

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: MiniSearch, with prefix and fuzzy matching switched on.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: It is small, has no dependencies and forgives the typos a volunteer makes with gloves on.

fields.label: Alternatives considered
fields.value: Lunr (no fuzzy matching on prefixes); writing our own substring match (no ranking).

items.title: One entry or one per item

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: A tool is one catalog entry with one or more copies.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: Members look for "a drill", volunteers hand over "drill number 2". Both need to be true at once.

blocks.heading: Photos
blocks.markdown: Photos are taken on the tablet, resized to 800 px on the long side before upload, and stored on the server disk. No decision is open here; the library already owns the disk.

items.title: Tool
items.markdown:
A kind of thing the library lends.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | |
| name | text | "Tile cutter" |
| category_id | uuid | references Category |
| purpose | text[] | words members search by: "tiles", "bathroom" |
| photo_path | text | nullable |
| retired_at | timestamptz | nullable; hidden from search when set |

items.title: Copy
items.markdown:
One physical item of a tool.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | |
| tool_id | uuid | references Tool |
| label_code | text | unique, printed on the item: `BB-0412` |
| shelf | text | "C3" |
| condition | enum | `ok`, `needs_repair`, `retired` |

items.title: Category
items.markdown:
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | |
| name | text | unique: "Garden", "Painting" |
| sort_order | int | order in the category list |

blocks.heading: Relationships
blocks.markdown:
- A Tool belongs to one Category.
- A Tool has one or more Copies.
- A Copy is lent, not a Tool (see `003-loan-checkout`).

blocks.heading: State Transitions
blocks.markdown:
```text
ok ──► needs_repair ──► ok
 │            │
 └────────────┴──► retired
```

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.markdown: Lending is the reason the library exists. Today a loan is a line in a paper book; this feature makes it a scan and a tap.

items.title: Lend a tool
items.narrative:
**As a** volunteer at the counter
**I want to** scan a member card and a tool label
**So that** the loan is recorded before the member leaves the desk

scenarios.given: a member with no overdue loans and a tool that is on the shelf
scenarios.when: I scan the member card and then the tool label
scenarios.then:
a loan is created with a due date two weeks from today

And the tool shows as "out" in the catalog

scenarios.given: a member who already holds five tools
scenarios.then: the loan is refused with the reason on screen

items.title: Take a tool back
items.narrative:
**As a** volunteer at the counter
**I want to** scan a returned tool
**So that** it is back in the catalog for the next member

scenarios.given: a tool that is on loan
scenarios.then:
the loan is closed with today's date

And the tool shows as "in" in the catalog

scenarios.given: a tool that comes back broken
scenarios.when: I mark it "needs repair" while returning it
scenarios.then:
the loan is closed and the tool cannot be lent

But the member is not blocked from borrowing

items.title: Extend a loan
items.narrative:
**As a** member
**I want to** extend my loan once from my phone
**So that** I do not have to come in when a job takes longer

scenarios.given: a loan that is not overdue and that nobody is waiting for
scenarios.then: the due date moves one week

scenarios.given: a loan that was extended before
scenarios.then: I am told to ask at the counter

items.text: System MUST create a loan from one member card scan and one tool label scan
System MUST set the due date to 14 days after checkout
System MUST refuse a loan when the member holds five tools or has an overdue loan
System MUST close a loan when the tool label is scanned at return
System MUST let a member extend a loan once by 7 days
System MUST record checkouts and returns while offline and sync them in order
A checkout takes at most three taps after the two scans
No loan is lost when the tablet loses power between scan and sync

blocks.heading: Out of Scope
blocks.markdown:
- Deposits and fines
- Reserving a tool that is on the shelf

blocks.heading: Summary
blocks.markdown: Loans are an append-only list of events (checked out, extended, returned) written on the tablet first and replayed on the server, so two tablets that were offline never disagree about who holds a tool.

meta.label: Input
meta.value: User description: "A third of the tools come back late, mostly because people forget. Remind them."

items.title: Reminder before the due date
items.why: Forgetting is the main cause of late returns; one message fixes most of it.
items.test: Create a loan due in two days, run the daily job, and see one message addressed to the member.

scenarios.given: a loan due in two days
scenarios.then: the member gets one message naming the tool and the due date

scenarios.given: a member with three loans due on the same day
scenarios.then: they get one message listing all three tools

scenarios.given: a loan that was already reminded
scenarios.when: the job runs again the same day
scenarios.then: no second message is sent

items.rest: A member gets a message two days before a tool is due, by the contact detail they gave at signup.

items.title: Overdue notice
items.why: Needed for the tools that still come back late, but it helps fewer members than the first reminder.
items.test: Let a loan pass its due date, run the job, and see the notice and the loan on the overdue list.

scenarios.given: a loan one day past its due date
scenarios.then: the member gets an overdue notice

scenarios.given: a loan that has been overdue for a week
scenarios.when: a volunteer opens the overdue list
scenarios.then: the loan is at the top with the member's contact detail

items.rest: A member whose tool is late gets a notice the day after, and the volunteers see the list of overdue loans.

items.title: Stop the reminders
items.why: Required by the "Ask for Less" principle, used by few.
items.test: Turn reminders off for a member, run the job, and see that nothing is sent to them.

scenarios.given: a member who turned reminders off
scenarios.when: one of their loans is due in two days
scenarios.then: no message is sent and the loan still appears on the volunteers' list

items.rest: A member who does not want messages turns them off.

items.text: System MUST send one reminder per member two days before a due date, listing every tool due that day
System MUST send one overdue notice the day after a missed due date
System MUST never send the same reminder twice
System MUST send by SMS when the member gave a phone number and by email otherwise
System MUST let a member turn reminders off with one tap from any message
System MUST show volunteers a list of overdue loans, oldest first
Late returns fall from 33% to under 15% within two months
Fewer than 1 in 100 members turns reminders off
The association pays less than 10 euros a month for messages

blocks.heading: Summary
blocks.markdown: A daily job on the server reads the loans due in two days and the loans that became overdue, groups them by member, and sends one message each through a small sender interface with an SMS and an email implementation. Every send is recorded, which is also what prevents a second one.

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: SMS when the member gave a phone number, email otherwise.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: Nine in ten members signed up with a phone number, and a text is read within minutes. Email costs nothing and covers the rest.

fields.label: Alternatives considered
fields.value: A messaging app bot (members would have to add a contact first); push notifications (there is no member app to push to); email only (half the members gave no address).

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: Two days before the due date, at 10:00 local time.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: Two days leaves a weekend day to bring the tool back, and 10:00 is inside the opening hours of both weekdays the library is open.

fields.label: Alternatives considered
fields.value: The evening before (too late to plan a trip); one week before (forgotten again by the due date).

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: An in-process cron schedule in the existing server.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: One job a day does not justify a queue or a second process.

fields.label: Alternatives considered
fields.value: A system cron entry calling an HTTP route (one more thing to configure on the server); a job queue (nothing else needs one yet).

fields.label: Decision
fields.value: A unique key on member, kind and due date in the `reminders` table; the row is written before the message is sent.

fields.label: Rationale
fields.value: If the job crashes and restarts, the key refuses the duplicate. A message that was recorded but not sent is retried by a separate sweep.

blocks.heading: Message cost
blocks.markdown: At the provider's price of 7 cents a text and about 110 reminders a month, the bill is close to 8 euros. Grouping loans per member, as FR-001 asks, is what keeps it under the 10 euro limit.

items.title: Reminder
items.markdown:
One message sent, or about to be sent, to one member.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | |
| member_id | uuid | references Member |
| kind | enum | `due_soon`, `overdue` |
| due_date | date | the due date the message is about |
| channel | enum | `sms`, `email` |
| status | enum | `pending`, `sent`, `failed` |
| sent_at | timestamptz | nullable |

Unique on (`member_id`, `kind`, `due_date`).

items.title: Reminder Preference
items.markdown:
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| member_id | uuid | primary key, references Member |
| enabled | boolean | default `true` |
| changed_at | timestamptz | |

blocks.heading: Relationships
blocks.markdown:
- A Reminder covers every loan of one member that shares its due date.
- A Reminder Preference belongs to exactly one Member; no row means reminders are on.

blocks.heading: State Transitions
blocks.markdown:
```text
pending ──► sent
   │
   └──► failed ──► pending   (retried up to 3 times by the sweep)
```
How to check this feature by hand once it is built.

blocks.heading: Prepare a loan that is due in two days
blocks.markdown:
```sh
npm run seed -- --member "Test Member" --phone "+31600000000"
npm run seed:loan -- --member "Test Member" --tool "Tile cutter" --due-in 2
```

blocks.heading: Run the daily job with the fake sender
blocks.markdown:
```sh
REMINDER_SENDER=fake npm run reminders:run
```

Expected output:

```text
due_soon  Test Member  sms  "Your Tile cutter is due back on Saturday 16 May."
1 reminder sent, 0 skipped, 0 failed
```

blocks.heading: Run it again
blocks.markdown:
```sh
REMINDER_SENDER=fake npm run reminders:run
```

Nothing is sent the second time: `0 reminders sent, 1 skipped, 0 failed`.

blocks.heading: Turn reminders off and check
blocks.markdown: Open the link from the message, tap "Stop reminders", create another loan for the same member and run the job once more. The loan appears in the volunteers' list at `/counter/overdue` when it is late, but no message is recorded.

blocks.heading: Message texts to review
blocks.markdown:
| Kind | English | Dutch |
|---|---|---|
| Due soon | Your {tools} is due back on {date}. | Je {tools} moet terug op {date}. |
| Overdue | Your {tools} was due on {date}. Please bring it back this week. | Je {tools} had terug moeten zijn op {date}. Breng je het deze week terug? |

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Borrowbox reminders
  version: 0.1.0
paths:
  /counter/overdue:
    get:
      summary: Overdue loans, oldest first
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The list shown to volunteers
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/OverdueLoan'
  /members/{memberId}/reminders:
    put:
      summary: Turn reminders on or off for one member
      parameters:
        - name: memberId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid

        required: true
        content:

            schema:
              type: object
              required: [enabled]
              properties:

                  type: boolean
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Saved
        '404':
          description: No such member

          type: string

          type: string

          type: string
          format: date

          type: integer

blocks.heading: Overview
blocks.markdown: The pressure washer and the two ladders are almost never on the shelf. Members ask the volunteers to "call me when it's back", and the volunteers keep sticky notes. This feature replaces the sticky notes.

items.title: Join the waitlist
items.narrative:
**As a** member
**I want to** put my name down for a tool that is out
**So that** I do not have to keep checking whether it came back

scenarios.given: a tool with every copy on loan
scenarios.when: I tap "tell me when it's back"
scenarios.then:
I am added to the end of the waitlist for that tool

And I see my place in the queue

scenarios.given: a tool that is on the shelf
scenarios.then: there is no waitlist button

items.title: Be told when it is back
items.narrative:
**As a** member on a waitlist
**I want to** get a message when the tool is returned
**So that** I can come and borrow it

scenarios.given: I am first on the waitlist for a tool
scenarios.when: a copy of it is returned
scenarios.then:
I get a message saying it is held for me for three days

And the copy cannot be lent to anyone else during those days

scenarios.given: I do not collect the tool within three days
scenarios.then:
the next member on the waitlist is told

But I keep my membership without any penalty

items.title: See who is waiting
items.narrative:
**As a** volunteer
**I want to** see the waitlist of a tool when it is returned
**So that** I put it on the hold shelf instead of the normal one

scenarios.given: a returned tool with a waitlist
scenarios.then: the screen says "hold for" and the first member's name

items.text: System MUST let a member join the waitlist of a tool only when no copy is available
System MUST keep the waitlist in the order members joined
System MUST hold a returned copy for the first waiting member for three days
System MUST tell the next member when a hold ends without a loan
System MUST show the hold on the return screen
No sticky notes on the counter after one month
80% of holds end in a loan

meta.label: Input
meta.value: User description: "Tools come back broken and nobody knows since when. Let people report damage, with a photo."

items.title: Report damage at return
items.why: Most damage is noticed at the counter, and the repair volunteers need to know what to fix.
items.test: Return a tool, add a damage report with a photo, and see it on the repair list.

scenarios.given: a tool being returned
scenarios.when: the volunteer taps "damaged" and takes a photo
scenarios.then: a damage report is saved and the tool is marked "needs repair"

scenarios.given: a tool with an open damage report
scenarios.then: it is shown as not available

items.rest: A volunteer who takes back a damaged tool records what is wrong, with a photo, before it goes to the repair shelf.

items.title: Report damage from home
items.why: It gives the repair volunteers a head start, and members would rather say so than be found out.
items.test: Open a current loan on a phone, report damage, and see the report at the counter.

scenarios.given: a member with a tool on loan
scenarios.when: they send a damage report from their phone
scenarios.then: the volunteers see it on the repair list before the tool is back

scenarios.given: a member who reports damage
scenarios.then: they see a message that says what happens next [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: does the member pay for repairs, and does the message say so?]

items.rest: A member who breaks a tool, or finds it broken, reports it from their phone before bringing it back.

items.title: Close a repair
items.why: Without it, tools stay on the repair shelf in the catalog forever.
items.test: Close a report as "fixed" and find the tool available again in search.

scenarios.given: an open damage report
scenarios.when: a repair volunteer marks it fixed
scenarios.then: the tool is available again

scenarios.given: an open damage report
scenarios.when: a repair volunteer marks it beyond repair
scenarios.then: the tool is retired and keeps its history

items.rest: A repair volunteer marks a tool as fixed, or as beyond repair.

blocks.heading: Edge Cases
blocks.markdown:
- Damage that was already there: the previous borrower returned it without anyone noticing.
- A report with no photo because the tablet camera is broken.

items.text: System MUST let a volunteer attach a damage report with a description and a photo to a tool at return
System MUST let a member report damage on a tool they currently hold
System MUST mark a tool with an open damage report as not available
System MUST keep damage photos for [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: how long may photos be kept under the "Ask for Less" principle?]
System MUST let a repair volunteer close a report as fixed or beyond repair
System MUST notify [NEEDS CLARIFICATION: who is told about a new report, every repair volunteer or one coordinator?]

blocks.heading: Key Entities
blocks.markdown: - **Damage Report**: what is wrong with one copy of a tool; description, photo, who reported it, when, and how it was closed

items.text: Every tool on the repair shelf has a report that says what is wrong
Half of the damaged tools are available again within two weeks

meta.label: Input
meta.value: User description: "Due dates land on days we are closed. Show the opening hours and never set a due date on a closed day."

items.title: Due dates on open days only
items.why: A due date on a closed day makes a member late through no fault of their own.
items.test: Lend a tool so that 14 days later is a closed day, and see the due date moved to the next open day.

scenarios.given: the library is closed on Sundays
scenarios.when: a loan would be due on a Sunday
scenarios.then: its due date is the following open day

scenarios.given: a holiday closure entered by a volunteer
scenarios.when: a loan would be due inside it
scenarios.then: its due date is the first open day after the closure

items.rest: A loan is never due on a day the library is closed.

items.title: See when the library is open
items.why: It saves a trip, but the hours are also on the door.
items.test: Enter a closure for next week and see it on the catalog page.

scenarios.given: a closure next Saturday
scenarios.then: a notice names the day the library is closed

items.rest: A member sees the opening hours and upcoming closures on the catalog page.

items.text: System MUST store the weekly opening hours and single-day closures
System MUST move a due date that falls on a closed day to the next open day
System MUST show the opening hours and the next closure on the catalog page
No loan is due on a closed day
